title: Abstraction Ladder Diagram
description: Five implementation approaches ranked as a ladder with illustrative relative execution times, each clickable to reveal what runs the code, how values are represented, and what that rung costs.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Programming Languages
Optimization

learningObjectives: Organize five approaches into a ranked ladder
Differentiate what each rung gives up for speed
Choose a rung appropriate to a stated constraint

controls.label: Any rung
controls.purpose: Show runner, value representation, and what it costs

assumptions: Bar lengths are illustrative relative times, labeled as such on the canvas
Ordering reflects the typical case; specific workloads vary
limitations: Ratios are indicative rather than measured; the chapter's own benchmarks supply real figures

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Ranked ladder with a cost column beside the speed column
keyQuestions: At which rung does the value representation change?
Which loss would matter most to your project?
commonMisconceptions: That faster is always better regardless of what is given up
That the largest speedup requires leaving Python
assessmentOpportunities: Select a rung for a stated deadline miss and maintainability constraint
